subsystems.name: Nuclear heat source
subsystems.role: supplies low-pressure steam and electricity to the desalination plant.

subsystems.name: Isolation loop
subsystems.role: keeps radioactive coolant entirely separate from the product water.

subsystems.name: Thermal desalination train
subsystems.role: evaporates and condenses seawater in repeated stages, using low-grade steam.

subsystems.name: Membrane train (hybrid option)
subsystems.role: reverse osmosis driven by nuclear electricity instead of steam.

subsystems.name: Seawater intake and outfall
subsystems.role: brings seawater in and returns concentrated brine to the sea.

subsystems.name: Product water conditioning
subsystems.role: makes the water drinkable or suitable for irrigation.

buildSteps.title: Size the heat and water demand
buildSteps.detail: decide how much steam can be bled from the turbine without hurting electricity output, and how much water the region needs.

buildSteps.title: Design the coupling
buildSteps.detail: set steam pressure and temperature at the extraction point, and place an intermediate loop so plant water can never enter the product.

buildSteps.title: Build intake and outfall
buildSteps.detail: lay a screened intake offshore and a diffuser that mixes brine back into the sea quickly.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate evaporator stages
buildSteps.detail: large steel vessels with thousands of tubes are built and erected on site in series, each at a lower pressure than the last.

buildSteps.title: Add membrane trains if hybrid
buildSteps.detail: reverse-osmosis racks are installed alongside, so cheap off-peak nuclear electricity can boost output.

buildSteps.title: Install the isolation loop
buildSteps.detail: heat exchangers and monitoring instrumentation are fitted and pressure-tested.

buildSteps.title: Commission
buildSteps.detail: systems are leak-tested, evacuated, filled with seawater, and the first water is discarded until quality is proven.

buildSteps.title: Run and monitor
buildSteps.detail: operators track water chemistry, radioactivity and brine salinity continuously through decades of operation.

prerequisites.why: they provide the steady steam and electricity that desalination needs.
proven large-scale thermal methods that can run on steam too cool for turbines.
the cheapest desalination route when driven by electricity rather than heat.
the product water must be provably free of radioactive carry-over.
warm, salty discharge can harm seabeds if poorly sited or diffused.

pathway.milestone: small coupled plants — the BN-350 at Aktau in Kazakhstan supplied city water for decades, and the Kalpakkam plant in India has run since the early 2000s
pathway.unlocks: proof that nuclear heat and membranes can deliver drinking water.

pathway.milestone: purpose-built cogeneration reactors sized to a city's water demand
pathway.unlocks: water security for arid coastal regions without fossil fuel.

pathway.milestone: floating or barge-mounted nuclear desalination for islands
pathway.unlocks: fresh water where there is no grid or coastline infrastructure.

pathway.milestone: small modular reactors dedicated to water and heat
pathway.unlocks: lower capital cost and wider deployment beyond large coastal grids.
